source.title: A developmental increase of inhibition promotes the emergence of hippocampal ripples

confidence_rationale: This is a causal (optogenetic/chemogenetic), mechanistic demonstration that hippocampal sharp-wave ripples -- the substrate of replay -- do not simply appear at birth but require a specific developmental prerequisite (maturation of CA1 inhibitory circuitry) to emerge, and that manipulating that prerequisite directly (silencing interneurons) reduces ripple rate. This is close to direct mechanistic support for MECH-533's joint/conditional claim: offline replay competence is not available from the start and depends on a maturational process distinct from mere exposure or frequency of offline windows, which is precisely the 'replay hardware maturation gate' DEV-NEED-029 names.
failure_signatures: This is rodent (mouse) electrophysiology at very early postnatal ages (4-12 days) using optogenetic/chemogenetic causal manipulation of inhibitory interneurons directly -- the causal lever (silencing CA1 interneurons) has no direct REE analogue; REE's replay-competence maturation would need its own substrate-level account of what plays the inhibition-maturation role.

The study measures RIPPLE EMERGENCE (whether the oscillatory event occurs at all) rather than replay SEQUENCE FIDELITY or reorganisation competence specifically -- it grounds the coarser 'replay-capable hardware exists yet' half of MECH-533's joint claim, complementary to the finer-grained sequence-fidelity maturation shown in the Noguchi (2023) entry in this same directory.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Using in vivo electrophysiology combined with optogenetic and chemogenetic manipulation in 4-12-day-old mice, the authors show that hippocampal sharp-wave ripples -- previously undetectable -- can be robustly induced by light stimulation of CA1 pyramidal neurons only from postnatal day 10 onward, and that this emergence is mechanistically linked to the maturation of inhibitory input: chemogenetically silencing CA1 interneurons reduces ripple rate, and a spiking neural network model mechanistically connects inhibition maturation to ripple emergence.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-533 claims offline frequency and offline COMPETENCE co-mature -- frequent early offline windows are needed because traces are fragile while the offline-processing machinery itself (replay selection, sequence fidelity, cross-episode aggregation, re-indexing) is still immature, so any benefit of offline-window frequency is conditional on competence, and the two must be crossed rather than treated as independent factors. Pochinok et al. provide a causal, mechanistic grounding for the COMPETENCE half of this claim at its most basic level: the neural hardware capable of generating replay-supporting ripple events does not exist from birth, but emerges via a specific, experimentally-manipulable maturational process (inhibitory circuit development). This is strong support for treating replay competence as something that must mature rather than being assumed present whenever an offline window occurs.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This paper establishes that ripple-GENERATING hardware matures -- the coarsest possible reading of 'replay competence.' It does not itself measure whether the CONTENT of ripples (spike sequence fidelity, cross-episode aggregation) is competent once ripples begin occurring -- that finer-grained maturation is the subject of the companion Noguchi (2023) entry in this same directory. Read together, the two papers jointly ground MECH-533's competence axis at two different levels of the offline-processing pipeline.
mapping.source_context: Mouse; postnatal days 4-12; in vivo electrophysiology combined with optogenetic (channelrhodopsin-2) and chemogenetic manipulation of CA1 pyramidal neurons and interneurons; spiking neural network modeling for mechanistic interpretation.

confidence_components.notes: Very high source quality: a causal (not merely correlational) mechanistic study in a strong venue, directly establishing that replay-supporting neural hardware matures rather than being present from birth. Mapping fidelity moderate: grounds the coarsest reading of MECH-533's competence axis (hardware exists yet vs. not) rather than the finer content-fidelity reading, which the companion Noguchi entry addresses; transfer risk reflects the early-postnatal-rodent-to-REE-agent domain gap.
